causalChain: Broad professional hubs report Chinese/global trade recovery.
China-generalist reporting identifies export orders rising faster than available shipping capacity, with container and slot shortages.
Global wire reporting independently confirms the container shortage and unusually strong Chinese export growth.
The profit pool can therefore transfer not only to ocean carriers, but also to container-equipment suppliers; labor shortages create a separate second-order automation response.

validatedExpressions.name: 中远海控

evidence.claim: Q3 volumes and trans-Pacific volumes increased; first-nine-month net profit rose about 57% year on year.
Export demand, container/slot scarcity and freight rates had risen sharply; shipping-company profits were described as surging.

validatedExpressions.associationValue: obvious first-order beneficiary; useful control for less-obvious expressions

validatedExpressions.name: 中集集团

evidence.claim: Industry participants reported new-container orders already filled into the period after the 2021 Spring Festival.
CIMC orderbooks were filled through the end of Q1 2021 as carriers sought more boxes; Q3 profitability had recovered strongly.
China's November exports surged while a severe global container shortage pushed cargo costs to record highs.

validatedExpressions.associationValue: important non-obvious expression found by following the bottleneck one step upstream from shipping

validatedExpressions.name: 汇川技术

evidence.claim: Export manufacturers faced worker shortages and some were investing in automation/capacity to meet orders.
Inovance Q3 revenue and attributable profit had already accelerated strongly year on year.

validatedExpressions.associationValue: less-obvious cross-industry inference; do not promote merely because automation is a plausible response

rejectedShortcuts: Do not assume all exporters benefit: freight, FX and raw-material costs can absorb the order boom.
Do not treat ports/logistics as automatic beneficiaries without pricing-power evidence.
Do not promote automation suppliers until customer/order evidence shows the export/labor shock actually converts to orders.
